title: Molecular-level insight into water adsorption and projected atmospheric water harvesting performance in a hydrolytically stable MOF
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76301-0

A hydrolytically stable metal-organic framework enables direct visualisation of stepwise water adsorption at the molecular level, providing design insight for efficient, low-energy atmospheric water harvesting materials.

title: Ultrafast electron acceleration by space chorus
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76485-5

Chorus waves are thought to cause strong electron acceleration altering space weather, yet its fundamental physics remain unclear. Here, the authors present observational evidence for highly nonlinear, ultrafast chorus-induced electron acceleration.

title: Electrical control of exchange bias in sub-10 nm regime enabled by single-nanotube patterning
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76524-1

Li et al. demonstrate spin orbit torque driven switching of exchange bias in sub-10 nm devices, enabled by nanotube-based patterning. They show that exchange bias stabilizes ferromagnetic layers and can be dynamically switched by electric current.

title: Nuclear localization of the glutaminyl-tRNA synthetase QARS reveals its role in DNA damage response in ovarian cancer
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76046-w

Here, the authors find that the glutaminyl-tRNA synthetase QARS, a cytosolic protein involved in mRNA translation, relocates to the nucleus to promote homologous recombination (HR). QARS promotes HR by interacting with SP100 to maintain PML-NB integrity and MRN complex localization, thus reducing tumor sensitivity to treatment.

title: Iron Oxide Photoanode for Glycerol-Assisted Hydrogen Production at 8.87 mA cm<sup>–2</sup>
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75977-8

Iron oxide photoanodes are promising for solar hydrogen production but suffer from poor charge transport and slow water oxidation kinetics. Here, the authors report that Ge and Ti co-doped hematite enables glycerol-assisted photoelectrochemical hydrogen production with a photocurrent of 8.87 mA cm⁻².

title: In situ electron microscopy of LaNiO<sub>3</sub> transformation during reduction and methane dry reforming
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76419-1

This study presents the decomposition of LaNiO3, a model methane dry reforming catalyst using in situ electron microscopy. Intermediate phase formation is monitored on the atomic scale under different gas atmospheres and oxygen partial pressure regimes.

title: Decomposition and separation of vibration waves from blasting demolition of tall buildings and their component characteristics
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76458-8

This study introduces a three-dimensional polarisation analysis method to deconstruct vibration waves from building blasting demolition, enabling separation of P, S, and R waves. Results reveal stage- and direction-dependent wave dominance, improving assessment and control of vibration hazards.
